## Versioning and release tiers — managed by `publication`

**Do not hand-edit this block.** It is regenerated by `pub policy`. Canonical
source: `publication/VERSIONING.md` and `publication/RELEASE.md`.

### Version format

```
public release   MAJOR.MINOR.0
dev build        MAJOR.MINOR.0+g<short-sha>
```

* **The patch slot is always `0`.** Bump `MINOR` freely — that is the knob meant
  for constant motion. Public tags are therefore always `vMAJOR.MINOR.0`.
* **The commit sha goes in SemVer build metadata (`+g…`), never the patch slot.**
  This is not a style preference; it was verified against Cargo:
  * `0.61.0+g9d1ce1d2` satisfies `version = "0.61"`, `"0.61.0"` and `"=0.61.0"`.
  * `0.61.0-dev.2188+g9d1ce1d2` (a pre-release) satisfies **none** of them —
    a pre-release forces every dependent manifest to opt in explicitly.
  * A hash in the patch slot (`0.61.164757458`) is collision-free but makes
    versions move **backwards**, so Cargo reads later builds as downgrades.
* **Never mint a version from a dirty tree.** `pub version` appends `.dirty`;
  that is not publishable.

### Commands

```sh
pub version [repo] --release   # 0.4.0     — what alabsystems tags
pub version [repo] --dev       # 0.4.0+g1a2b3c4d5
pub bump    [repo] --minor --commit
pub check   [repo]             # local build/test gate (no CI, no Actions)
pub doctor  [repo]             # constellation invariants — run before promoting
pub cycle   --all              # pull -> doctor -> stage, then print the promote queue
```

### Tiers — who may write where

| Tier | Repo | Who writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dev | `<dev-org>/<repo>` | humans **and agents**, push `main` freely |
| staging | `<dev-org>/<repo>-staging` | agents, via `pub stage` |
| release | `alabsystems/<repo>` | agents, via `pub promote` (release credential + explicit `PUBLISH_RELEASE_REMOTE`) |

`<dev-org>` is the private development owner. It is named in the private
`publication` registry only — never in a repo that gets published, because this
block ships in public snapshots.

`pub promote` pushes the audited staging tree straight to public `main` — no
PR, no review branch, no TTY, and it does **not** refuse a non-interactive
caller. Agents run it. What authorizes the write is possession of the release
credential plus an explicit `PUBLISH_RELEASE_REMOTE` that promote verifies
against the registry's release slug before any push (KEYS.md owner decision
2026-08-23). If a public repo looks empty, the snapshot is sitting in
`<repo>-staging` and simply has not been promoted yet.

This paragraph previously said promotion was humans-only and that agents must
not attempt it. That was false — measured 2026-08-27, when ay 0.16.0 and aterm
0.62.0 were both promoted non-interactively — and it was orphaned text: its own
banner names `pub policy` as the generator, and that subcommand no longer
exists. A false control is worse than no control, because it stops the
automation it describes while providing none of the safety it claims.

### Two rules that keep breaking

1. **Never pin a public-facing reference to a dev-only sha.** `alabsystems/*`
   repos are snapshot repos with rewritten history; a dev commit does not exist
   there. `pub doctor` checks every submodule pin for reachability from a remote
   branch — run it before promoting.
2. **`publish/config.sh` must use flat `KEY_DEFAULT="value"` lines.** The engine
   reads the committed file with `^KEY_DEFAULT="(.*)"$` and does **not** source
   it, so `: "${KEY_DEFAULT:=…}"` parses in bash but is invisible to the engine.
